quotes.text: Use overcapture to capture more than the authorized amount for a PaymentIntent.
This article has multiple variants. Fetch one of the following URLs to view specific content for your use case:

old_evidence.text: If `unavailable`, the maximum_amount_capturable is the amount authorized.
If you’re on standard Stripe pricing and want access to this feature, contact us using the form at [Stripe support](https://support.stripe.com).

If you need to capture an amount larger than the `maximum_amount_capturable`, perform an [incremental authorization](https://docs.stripe.com/payments/incremental-authorization.md) to increase the authorized amount, where available.

findings: The November 7 capture retains the PaymentIntent overcapture definition and names three web UI variants at new raw lines 5-15. The May 11 capture contains all three variant bodies at old raw lines 8-224, 226-568 and 570-751. Only the May guide supplies the detailed behavior and prerequisites. Diff lines 3-12 and 748-754 show the body-to-index presentation change.

The May guide describes capturing above an online card authorization without an additional network authorization and says the customer's pending statement entry updates after settlement (old raw lines 12-26, 230-244, 574-586). Eligibility and caps depend on network, merchant country and category, issuer country and card type where applicable, with Diners Club US through Discover as limited beta. Visa's EEA exclusion concerns businesses, and Visa car-rental thresholds include local currency equivalent (old raw lines 28-60, 246-278, 588-620). Current summary lines 15-36 mostly preserve the table and need precise qualifiers.

In May, hosted and full embedded Checkout use server-created Checkout Sessions in mode=payment, with payment_intent_data.capture_method=manual according to the prose and payment_method_options.card.request_overcapture=if_available. Hosted uses the Session's URL and success_url. Full embedded uses ui_mode=embedded_page, the Session client_secret for browser mounting and return_url when configured. Advanced Elements uses a confirmed uncaptured PaymentIntent with capture_method=manual and the card request before or at confirmation (old raw lines 18-26, 79-149, 236-244, 297-350, 427-568, 637-664). Current summary lines 13-19 and 42-48 preserve the broad routes but conflate their request configuration.

After confirmation, inspect the associated latest_charge.payment_method_details.card.overcapture status and maximum_amount_capturable. If unavailable, the maximum falls back to the authorized amount. Capture the PaymentIntent with amount_to_capture within that cap. A successful capture changes PaymentIntent amount, amount_received and amount_capturable, while Charge card amount_authorized retains the original authorization. The illustrated transition is requires_capture to succeeded and the sample uses 1000 to 1200 (old raw lines 149-224, 350-425, 664-739). Current summary lines 44-50 omit the unavailable boundary and preserve the original amount field.

The old SCA sections apply when merchant and cardholder are in an SCA jurisdiction, generally require authenticating and authorizing at least the expected capture amount, and prescribe cancellation/re-creation if a higher amount is needed outside applicable exemptions. The source names absent-customer MIT as potentially exempt and distinguishes network obligations. The old test card table is sandbox evidence for network examples, not individual live transaction access (old raw lines 62-77, 280-295, 622-635 and 741-751). Current summary line 40 preserves a potential MIT exception, but loses 'generally' and the merchant/cardholder condition.
historical_claims_to_preserve: The 2026-05-11 full capture remains the authority here for online card and network/category/merchant-country/card-type rules, limited Diners Club beta, IC+ offering and standard pricing Support route, SCA scope and exemption qualifications, and the three dated integration variants (old raw lines 12-77, 230-295, 574-635).

Keep the May request and post-confirmation eligibility checks, amount and state boundaries, conditional incremental authorization fallback, and sandbox examples dated. Preserve hosted Checkout server/redirect versus full embedded server/client Session boundary and the Dahlia Stripe.js mounting example as May evidence (old raw lines 79-224, 297-568, 637-751).
conflicts: Both historical Checkout Session create examples include mode=payment and payment_method_options.card.request_overcapture=if_available but omit payment_intent_data.capture_method=manual, which the availability prose in the same two variants requires. The direct PaymentIntent sample does include capture_method=manual. Add a reciprocal warning in the source and Overcapture concept, with a Checkout concept route, so readers don't copy an incomplete hosted or embedded request (old raw lines 18-26, 108-147, 236-244, 307-348 and 637-662; Checkout concept line 126).

The old embedded UI return-page guide labels Checkout Session status complete as payment success, while the overcapture flow in that same variant can still leave the associated PaymentIntent in requires_capture with amount_received=0. Check the underlying PaymentIntent and Charge server-side and distinguish Session completion, successful capture and later statement/settlement effects (old raw lines 350-397 and 530-562). Add this boundary alongside the reciprocal warning for Checkout readers.

Source line 17 and Overcapture concept line 10 claim IC+ is strictly required. The retained May availability prose offers the feature to IC+ users and directs standard pricing users requesting access to Stripe Support. That supports a contact route, with no proof of standard-price approval or actual access (old raw lines 24-26, 242-244, 584-586). The Checkout concept's grouped IC+ only statement at line 118 likewise merits that overcapture-specific qualification.

Source line 50 and Overcapture concept line 60 present incremental authorization as an unconditional fallback. The May guide explicitly says where available (old raw lines 181-183, 382-384 and 696-698). The separately inspected May migration example requests both features and makes the two choices conditional on both being available on latest_charge after confirmation (raw/stripe-flexible-features-migration-2026.md:491-549).
unresolved_questions: The November variant bodies were outside this pinned capture. Current network limits, SCA application, actual account/transaction eligibility, behavior under any newer Stripe.js or API version, and settlement outcomes remain outside its evidence.

source_assessments.reason: The November capture only changes navigation. The existing May summary needs source-level corrections because it overstates pricing and fallback availability and omits a manual-capture prerequisite warning that matters when copying the linked Checkout examples.

answers.Q1: The November 7 capture at https://docs.stripe.com/payments/overcapture describes overcapture as capture above a PaymentIntent's authorized amount and routes readers to Stripe-hosted, full embedded and advanced Elements web variants (new raw lines 5-15). The mapped source-stripe-overcapture.md covers mechanics from the May 11 full guide. May describes eligible online card payments, IC+ availability with a Support route for standard pricing, network limits and SCA restrictions (old raw lines 12-77). Hosted and embedded variants start with a server-created Checkout Session in payment mode and require manual capture on the underlying PaymentIntent. The advanced integration uses a confirmed uncaptured PaymentIntent directly. The card request uses request_overcapture=if_available. After confirmation the associated latest Charge reports status and maximum_amount_capturable, which equals the authorized amount if overcapture is unavailable. Capture the PaymentIntent within the reported cap. In the successful example it transitions from requires_capture to succeeded and updates PaymentIntent amount, amount_received and amount_capturable, while the Charge retains amount_authorized. Checkout completion and later settlement are distinct from capture. The mapped summary conveys the core flow but omits the Checkout parameter distinction and understates the conditional eligibility boundaries (old raw lines 108-224, old raw lines 297-425 and old raw lines 637-739).
answers.Q2: At https://docs.stripe.com/payments/overcapture, the November capture is a navigation change. It retains the common definition and links the three variant URLs in place of their full bodies (new raw lines 5-15). Keep the May 11 mechanics in source-stripe-overcapture.md dated, including pricing, network/merchant/card limits and limited beta support, SCA and potential exemptions, server-side request and Charge status/cap inspection, the browser setup in the embedded path, and test-card examples (old raw lines 12-77, old raw lines 230-350, old raw lines 427-568 and old raw lines 637-751). Carry reciprocal source and concept warnings that the May hosted and embedded Session examples omit payment_intent_data.capture_method=manual despite the stated prerequisite, and that embedded Session completion can precede PaymentIntent capture. The old successful capture response and later statement update address different stages. Qualify the summary's IC+ only wording with the standard pricing Support route and retain that incremental authorization is a fallback only where available (old raw lines 22-26, old raw lines 108-149, old raw lines 179-196, old raw lines 236-244, old raw lines 307-397, old raw lines 530-562 and old raw lines 694-711). The variant links and sandbox examples establish no live eligibility, newer SDK behavior, capture success, settlement or compliance.
